desc:
Each element rects[i] = [w, h] describes the width and height of a rectangle. Two rectangles are interchangeable when their width-to-height ratios are equal, that is wi / hi == wj / hj as exact fractions.

Return the number of pairs (i, j) with i < j whose rectangles are interchangeable.

For example, [[4, 8], [3, 6], [10, 20], [15, 25]] gives 3: the first three rectangles all have ratio 1/2.
hints: Comparing the ratios of every two rectangles is O(n<sup>2</sup>). Is there a single value that identifies a ratio?
Dividing floating point numbers can make equal ratios look different. Use an exact canonical form instead.
Divide both sides by gcd(w, h) to get the reduced fraction (w/g, h/g). Equal ratios have equal reduced pairs, so count identical pairs with a hash map of reduced fractions.
editorial: Two fractions are equal exactly when they have the same reduced form, and the reduced form of w / h is (w / g, h / g) with g = gcd(w, h). This gives a hashable key without any floating point error.
Go through the rectangles, keep a map from key to the number of earlier rectangles with that key, and add that count to the answer before incrementing it. Time O(n log M) for the gcds, space O(n).
solution:
from math import gcd

def countEqualRatioPairs(rects):
    seen = {}
    total = 0
    for w, h in rects:
        g = gcd(w, h)
        key = (w // g, h // g)
        s = seen.get(key, 0)
        total += s
        seen[key] = s + 1
    return total
